statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 24: confirmed U.S. strikes on three Iranian crude carriers and the preceding Iranian missile attacks raise Sunday reopening-gap sensitivity, while the weekend NQ closure provides no live evidence of persistent one-way Nasdaq structure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; Tail remains below the block threshold. Stress is extreme from the direct U.S.-Iran exchange, constrained Gulf shipping, energy inflation pressure and Friday's higher-rate repricing. The next live price-path checkpoint is the Sunday futures reopening.
headline: U.S.-Iran tanker escalation keeps closed-market Nasdaq regime at WATCH
body: NQ is closed for the weekend. Reuters reports U.S. forces struck three Iranian crude carriers after Iranian missile attacks on two U.S. Navy ships. Friday's stronger jobs report lifted Treasury yields and left the Nasdaq 0.29% lower, while semiconductors outperformed. Shared Finviz context from 14:01 UTC is stale under the 90-minute rule and was not used as supporting evidence.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours include two orange Tail episodes during Friday live trading, subsequent normalization into the weekend closure, and a return to WATCH after the confirmed U.S.-Iran tanker and naval exchange. Since Friday's close, Tail has reflected discontinuity and reopening risk rather than observed persistent mean-reversion failure.
outlookSummary: NQ remains closed through all 24 forecast slots. If no additional verified U.S.-Iran or Hormuz escalation occurs, Tail is projected to ease within WATCH from 24 toward 20 as the strike shock ages; Stress remains extreme from conflict, energy and rate pressure. Sunday reopening at 22:00 UTC lies beyond this horizon and is the next live price-path checkpoint.
